pull.title: KAFKA-21228: Consider pending share updates in cold snapshot timer
pull.body:
Ref : https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21228

Problem : 

ShareCoordinatorShard.snapshotColdPartitions() skips a run when every share partition's last snapshot was written by the cold snapshot job. The code infers this from `createTimestamp != writeTimestamp`, since only cold snapshots keep the original `createTimestamp` and move `writeTimestamp`. `ShareUpdate` records do not change either of these timestamps. so once every partition was cold snapshotted the timer kept skipping, even after new updates arrived.

Two fixes:

- `snapshotColdPartitions()`: skip the run only if every partition is cold snapshotted and has no pending share updates. Partitions are still picked by time since the last snapshot alone. Idle partitions with no updates must keep being re-snapshotted, because the prune floor is the lowest latest-snapshot offset across all share partitions.

- `handleShareSnapshot()`: reset `snapshotUpdateCount` on every `ShareSnapshot`. Previously it was reset only once the threshold was reached, so after a cold or initialize snapshot it still counted updates the snapshot already contained. This made the next threshold snapshot come early, and the count could not be used as a pending-updates signal.
